task_brief: This is day 5 of "Algorithms, Loops, and Debugging". That is unit 4 in grade 4. Today is a mastery demonstration about simple variables. It takes about 40–60 minutes. It is one day's work, not the whole unit project. Your unit is working toward this: Build a short story, animation, or simple game using block-based logic and document the algorithm. Today helps by working on simple variables. Your unit also covers sequence review, events, loops and repeats, and conditionals: if-then. Today counts for a grade. Do it on your own.
primary_task: Show that you can do this on your own: simple variables. Put away the help sheet and the examples. Solve a new problem all the way. First write what answer you expect. Then test it two ways. Include one tricky case. Show what you expected and what you got. Then explain your thinking. Write it so someone new to simple variables could follow it. Everything you need is printed in activity_setup. It has the exact case, what should happen, how to try it, checks, and a paper choice worth the same score. Do not wait for another handout or app. Keep today's work tied to your unit. Today is about simple variables. It is part of "Algorithms, Loops, and Debugging". Later days in this unit cover other things, like sequence review. Before you stop, do this check: Rate confidence in simple variables, cite one piece of evidence from today, and choose: ready to extend, ready to review later, or need a different explanation. In grade 4, try the steps yourself before you ask for help. Give a reason in your own words for at least one choice. A labelled drawing or a spoken answer counts fully.

central_input.title: Inline simple variables code case
central_input.purpose: Use this exact fictional case to investigate simple variables; no other file, model, dataset, or account is needed.

expected_behavior_and_specification: The procedure must execute every supplied step in order; the main input must return open > check > save.
An empty step list must return an empty string, and a one-step list must retain that step.
The submitted explanation must connect the observed control flow or data state to simple variables, not merely state the final number.
The smallest test case must be tried and its actual result compared with the expected result.

execution_method.primary: No-install browser method: open any browser developer console, paste the complete starter code, press Enter, and record the output or exact error text.
execution_method.local_optional: If Node.js is already installed, save the unchanged snippet as activity.js and run `node activity.js`; installing Node.js is not required.
execution_method.no_computer_required: The hand-trace route below is a complete execution method and earns identical credit.

debugging_target.observed_failure: The main input should retain all three steps, but the unchanged program returns check > save.
debugging_target.target: Use the specification, unchanged run, and test table to locate the first divergent state or control-flow decision; explain the evidence before choosing an edit.
debugging_target.pre_attempt_support: Run and record the unchanged program, then diagnose and repair it independently from the specification and tests. No solution or worked repair is included in learner material.
debugging_target.scope_note: Diagnosing the state, control-flow, or data defect and connecting the repair to simple variables is the central evidence.

equal_credit_alternative.method: Paper or notes-app simulation; this earns exactly the same score as running code.
steps: Make one row for each statement or loop check and copy the starting input exactly.
Record every variable, object field, selected item, and output after that step.
Circle the first row where the actual state stops matching the specification.
Apply the one repair named in your explanation and trace all three tests again.
equal_credit_alternative.evidence_to_submit: The completed trace, the one-line corrected condition, and an expected-versus-actual table for all three tests.

test_or_check_criteria: You solved it with no help sheet and no examples in front of you.
You wrote what you expected first, then tested two ways including a tricky one.
Someone new to this could follow your explanation.
This is your own work. Nobody did a graded part for you.
No real password, real person, or real website appears anywhere.

presentation_and_privacy.sandbox_and_credentials_note: Everything in this task runs in a sandbox or on paper. Never use a real password, passphrase, API key, account credential, access token, precise home location, or any real person's identifiable information — invent fictional values instead. Do not sign into, probe, scan, stress, or attempt access to any live, production, school, or third-party system, and do not bypass a filter, licence, access control, or terms of service. Any practice login used in an example must be obviously invented — a silly made-up name paired with a nonsense multi-word phrase — and must never be anything you or anyone in your family actually uses somewhere real. If a task seems to need something real, substitute a made-up stand-in and note the substitution.

copyright_and_authorship: The graded submission must be your own authorship. A parent, tutor, or AI tool may explain an idea, demonstrate a technique, or give feedback on a draft, but must not produce, write, debug, or make any part of the work that is scored. Any code, asset, or text you did not write must be openly licensed or supplied for this task, and must be cited in a comment or note naming where it came from and what you changed.
accessibility_options: Provide readable text plus optional audio or read-aloud support; no voice feature is required.
Chunk directions into one action at a time and show a worked example or model.
Allow typed, handwritten, spoken, drawn, manipulatives-based, or demonstrated responses when the standard permits.
Offer reduced-copying, extended-time, hidden-timer, movement-break, and low-distraction options.
Use captions, alt text, high-contrast print, keyboard access, and text-only fallbacks for media.
Preserve the learning target while adjusting quantity, pacing, representation, or response mode.
task_accessibility_provisions: You can do this with the keyboard only, no mouse needed. Text can be made bigger, and you may do it on paper instead of a screen.
You can take a break, stretch, or come back to this later. That does not lower your score.
safety_and_privacy_rules: Allow a pause, break, or alternate response mode without treating it as failure.
Never require a real password, private message, precise location, account credential, API key, or identifiable image.
Use only fictional or sandboxed systems, accounts, and data; never probe, exploit, or attempt to access a real external system.
Use approved sites and tools; do not bypass filters, access controls, licensing, or terms of service.
Treat AI output as a draft to verify, not as an authority or a substitute for learner work.
The tutor may explain, demonstrate, or debug alongside the learner, but must not silently complete a graded project or assessment for them.

media.suggestion: Optional diagram, map, worked example, source image, demonstration, or short clip supporting simple variables.
media.fallback: Provide the same information as readable steps, alt text, transcript, tactile/concrete model, or teacher demonstration.

remediation: Reteaching for simple variables follows the signal actually observed, not a fixed script. If the signal is "prerequisite gap": Return to the smallest prerequisite needed for simple variables, model it with a concrete or text-only representation, then retry one fresh item. If the signal is "procedure without understanding": Ask the learner to explain or represent why the process for simple variables works before continuing. If the signal is "correct but low confidence": Confirm the reasoning specifically, offer one varied example of simple variables, and avoid unnecessary remediation. If the signal is "repeated error pattern": Name the observable pattern neutrally, contrast it with a worked example, and schedule a short same-day or next-session review. If the signal is "mastery evidence": Require accurate independent application plus explanation on a later or different occasion before marking simple variables mastered. Re-check with one fresh item of the same kind before moving on, and record which signal was seen so the pattern is visible across the unit rather than treated as a one-off.
extension: Apply simple variables under a new constraint, compare two approaches or perspectives, or teach the idea with an original example without completing another learner’s graded work. Treat this as optional depth on simple variables rather than extra volume: one harder case done well beats three more of the same. Extension work stays inside the same sandbox rules — no real credentials and no live external systems. Extension work is never required to reach mastery and must not be assigned as a penalty.
